rationale: Two patch findings confirmed against source: clearing a project's cost center without also resetting chargeback_attribution leaves it persisted as cost_center-attributed with no linked cost center, and chargeback_attribution accepts any unvalidated string that only fails at DB flush via an uncaught IntegrityError instead of a clean 400 (also the standards audit's blocking security-patterns row). All four lenses and the standards audit ran with parseable output and every candidate was verified against real source; 3 candidates were dismissed (a migration-backfill concern the spec explicitly rules a non-goal, an import/test-mock concern that checked out clean, and a feature-flag-default mismatch that matches the spec's intended disabled-by-default design) and 0 were deferred.

findings.title: Clearing cost center leaves stale cost_center attribution
findings.problem: update_project passes the caller-supplied chargeback_attribution parameter straight into _validate_chargeback_attribution without reconciling it against the project's already-persisted value. When clear_cost_center=True is sent without also passing chargeback_attribution="project", a project whose attribution was already "cost_center" keeps that value while cost_center_id is set to None.
findings.impact: The project ends up persisted with chargeback_attribution="cost_center" and no linked cost center - a cross-field inconsistency the CHECK constraint does not catch (it only restricts the two string values). The same call shape also bypasses the projectChargeback feature-flag gate, since that gate only fires when chargeback_enabled or chargeback_attribution is explicitly set on the request.
findings.recommendation: In _validate_chargeback_attribution, check the effective attribution (chargeback_attribution if not None else project.chargeback_attribution) against resolved_cost_center_id instead of only the raw parameter, so a cost-center-clearing update that would leave an existing "cost_center" attribution orphaned is rejected.

findings.title: Chargeback attribution accepts unvalidated strings
findings.problem: ProjectUpdateRequest.chargeback_attribution (projects.py:266) is a bare Optional[str], and _validate_chargeback_attribution (project_service.py:299-312) only branches when the value is exactly "cost_center"; any other non-null string (a typo, wrong case, or arbitrary value) skips all application-level validation.
findings.impact: The invalid value is forwarded to application_repository.update_project, which unconditionally assigns it to the ORM object; it is rejected only at session.flush() by the new ck_applications_chargeback_attribution CHECK constraint. The PATCH /projects/{projectName} handler has no IntegrityError catch (confirmed: only create_project catches it), so a bad client value surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of a clean 400 - the same gap the standards audit flags as a partial security-patterns violation.
findings.recommendation: Constrain chargeback_attribution to Literal["project", "cost_center"] on ProjectUpdateRequest, or explicitly reject any value not in {"project", "cost_center"} inside _validate_chargeback_attribution with the existing ExtendedHTTPException(code=400, ...) before it reaches the repository.
